title: Transit Guide
summary: An offline route-instruction interface designed with blind and low-vision riders for disrupted public transit.
intended_users: Blind and low-vision riders navigating temporary platform, elevator, and route changes with unreliable connectivity.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: The project traces bounded access constraints and rejected visual-only alternatives into explicit route-instruction and disruption behavior.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: The committed alternatives table compares benefits, rejected costs, and the condition that triggers reconsideration.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Route facts, access preferences, instruction generation, disruption policy, and semantic rendering are isolated.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Static evidence cannot verify behavior with every browser and assistive-technology combination.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Mark an inaccessible path unavailable and produce a bounded alternative when facts permit. Avoid inventing landmarks and retain step ordering with explicit uncertainty. Reject route text containing markup or unsupported executable content.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Static evidence cannot verify behavior with every browser and assistive-technology combination. Generated guidance remains constrained by the accuracy and timeliness of supplied transit facts.

testing_strategy: Committed cross-boundary, negative, and boundary tests: test/disruption-boundaries.test.js, test/access-needs.test.js. Their presence does not establish that they pass in Finch static review.
security_threat: Malformed or injected route data produces misleading or unsafe instructions. Control: A strict validator bounds route facts, rejects external markup, and requires safety-critical fields. Sensitive access preferences or location history are retained beyond guide generation. Control: The guide accepts bounded preferences per request and emits no persistent identity or history fields.
production_limitation: Static evidence cannot verify behavior with every browser and assistive-technology combination. Generated guidance remains constrained by the accuracy and timeliness of supplied transit facts.
technical_debt: Complete deployment-specific runtime, performance, accessibility, and security evaluation before production use.
track_alignment_explanation: The product primarily improves transit autonomy for defined visual, mobility, and cognitive-load access needs.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.

ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.
